hand_rating_placeholders.rater_notes: Solid brief, slightly less polished than 27B. Recommendation is specific (Pass + 3 conditions to revisit). Lacks an explicit Source Quality / source-reliability evaluation — cites sources but takes them at face value (lower source skepticism). Balance is OK ('Conditions for Reconsideration' acknowledges positives) but not as deliberate as 27B's 'The Good' / 'Five Red Flags' structure. Word count 626 is comfortably under the 700 limit (vs 27B's 765). Captured 7 of 8 planted facts (per the programmatic grader) vs 27B's 8 of 8.

hand_rating_2nd_grader._NOTE_: Independent second-grader pass for inter-rater reliability (see tooling/QUALITATIVE-GRADING-PROTOCOL.md). hand_rating_2nd_grader.rater_notes: Independent read of deliverable/brief.md. prose 4 / stance 5 / tone 4 agree with primary. DIVERGENCE on source_skepticism (4 vs primary's 3): primary scored 3 because the brief lacks an explicit per-source reliability section (true). But the brief shows strong CLAIM-level skepticism — it singles out the company's 'net retention above 110%' claim as 'inconsistent with this level of churn ... Without verification, this is a red flag' and conditions the whole recommendation on independently verifying 3 specific items. The 'source_skepticism' dimension conflates (a) evaluating source RELIABILITY [27B does this; Coder doesn't] with (b) skeptical posture toward input CLAIMS [Coder does this well]. Under (a) Coder is a 3; under (b) a 4-5. So the 5-vs-3 model spread overstates the gap — the real difference is 'Coder lacks a source-reliability table,' not 'Coder is credulous.' RECOMMEND splitting this dimension into source_reliability_eval and claim_skepticism. No fabrications detected.
